title: "H07: Latitude, photoperiod, and possible exposure plateaus"
params:
  placement: glasses
  scenario: primary

## What this notebook checks

Assess whether exposure stops increasing beyond some latitude or photoperiod.
Photoperiod is the daylight duration between dawn and dusk. A levelling-off
would be described as a plateau, rather than assumed to be a ceiling. Separate
the roles of site, latitude, photoperiod, and the dates or seasons in which
each site was measured. Do not choose outcomes based on H02 results.

## What this notebook uses and produces

- Uses: the prepared H07 dataset in `artifacts/06_model_data/H07.rds`.
- Produces: if a plateau can be estimated, its definition, size, and
  uncertainty; otherwise, a clear statement that the available data cannot
  identify one. The notebook also produces fitted models, model checks,
  practical summaries with 95% confidence intervals, the exact participants,
  participant-days, observations, and sites used by each model, overall and by
  site; tables, figures, and source data.
- Data sensitivity: fit this identical H07 implementation to the
  manuscript-prepared dataset and compare exact samples, estimates, 95%
  confidence intervals, diagnostics, plateau conclusions, and overall
  stability.
